title: Bluegate Tenant Protection Plan Claims Manual: Coverage on the Loss Date, Perils, Deadlines and Documents
content:
## 1. Coverage in force on the loss date

A claim on a Bluegate Tenant Protection Plan is decided on the coverage in force on the loss date: the plan must have been past its effective date and not lapsed, cancelled or terminated on that date. A claim is covered only when the plan was in force on the loss date, judged from the plan's effective, lapse, cancellation and termination dates and its change history.

## 2. Perils

The loss must come from a covered peril of the level. A loss from an excluded peril is denied for an excluded peril. Climate-control damage is covered only on levels where climate-control failure is covered, and only when the facility has logged the climate-control failure.

## 3. Filing deadline

A claim is accepted only when it is filed not later than the discovery date plus the level's claim filing period. The filing period counts calendar days starting the day after the discovery date, and the last counted day is included. A late claim is denied as filed late.

*Boundary (hypothetical, filing period of 60 days):* discovery on day 0; a claim filed on day 60 is accepted; a claim filed on day 61 is filed late.

## 4. Burglary and vandalism

For burglary or vandalism, a police report filed within the level's police-report period of the discovery date is required, and burglary also needs forced-entry evidence where the level requires it; a lock cut by the company during the lien process is never forced entry.

| Claim | Police report in time | Forced-entry evidence | Meets this section |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| vandalism | yes | not required | yes |
| vandalism | no | — | no |
| burglary | yes | door or wall damage, or a lock cut by a third party | yes |
| burglary | yes | only a lock cut by the company in the lien process | no |
| burglary | no | — | no |

## 5. Documents

A claimed amount above the level's inventory threshold needs an itemized inventory with proof of ownership, and above the level's adjuster-inspection threshold an adjuster inspection, before a decision. A missing document is asked for once per document; if it is not received within the level's document-response period the claim is denied for documents not received.

## 6. Property

Cash, securities and personal papers are excluded where the level does not cover them, vehicles and their contents where the level does not cover them, and property held for others where the level does not cover it, while household members' property is covered where the level covers it.

## 7. Reporting

The loss must be reported to the facility office within the level's facility-notice period of discovery, photographs are required where the level requires them, the itemized proof of loss must arrive within the level's proof-of-loss period of filing, and claims are filed through the level's claim filing channels.

## Evidence

Every point is judged from the company's records of the claim (loss, discovery and filing dates, peril, police report number and date, forced-entry evidence, documents asked for) and of the plan (effective, lapse, cancellation and termination dates and change history).
